items.title: Brian Venturo’s founder story, CoreWeave
items.summary: Brian Venturo, CoreWeave co-founder, shares his story of building the company from a single, small warehouse to the essential cloud for AI. Shot on site in CoreWeave’s original modest location, Brian reminisces on early challenges and walks through his philosophy on what it takes to be a successful founder in today’s AI-dominant world. Brian shares how his personal experience as a co-founder inspired the creation of ARENA, CoreWeave’s production-ready AI lab, purpose-built for validating real models and pipelines before going live. He invites all founder-hopefuls to test their ideas on ARENA.

items.title: OpenAI & Google Sued: Are AI Giants Building Illegal "Public Nuisances"?

items.title: Gemini Decision 1: You Don’t Need an LLM to Make a Decision
items.summary: Gemini Decision 1 is Google's new decision model: it answers yes/no, multiple-choice and score questions about text, images, audio, PDFs and video, and returns a probability and a confidence score instead of generating text. In this video I show how the Gemini Decisions API works, how to call it in Python with every input type, where a decision model makes more sense than an LLM, and four mistakes I made while building three apps with it. 🔗 Code (quickstart, notebook and the three apps): https://github.com/PromtEngineer/gemini-decisions-codelab Sources: Google's announcement: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemini-decisions-api/ Decisions API docs: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api Gemini Decision 1 model page: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models/gemini-decision-1 Related videos: Needle 3: You Don't Need an LLM for Function Calling: https://youtu.be/qbN559fQn7k Build RAG with JEV: https://youtu.be/UhGH8cNG0qs Chapters: 00:00 What Gemini Decision 1 Does 01:43 How Decision Models Differ From LLMs 03:11 Yes/No, Choice and Score Questions 04:36 Best Use Cases for Decision Models 06:14 Cost: Decision Model vs Gemini Flash 07:23 Build With the Gemini Decisions API 09:10 Image, Audio, PDF and Video Inputs 10:59 Add an Other Option to Choice Questions 12:15 Send Only What the Question Needs 14:10 Ask Small Questions in a Browser Agent 16:02 Build a Voice Agent With Audio Input #Gemini #DecisionModels #aiagents Disclosure: I work at Google. This video is based on public information, the code is a personal, unofficial project, and the views are my own.

items.title: Former Google Researchers Just Built the Ultimate Indian Voice AI

items.title: The Same Gut Microbe Can Help or Hurt You
items.summary: In episode 1043 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Dr. Guru Banavar, Founding CTO at Viome, how the same gut microbe can have vastly different effects on your health depending on which genes are being expressed. Dr. Banavar explains that knowing the presence of a microbe like Akkermansia muciniphila isn't enough; understanding its gene expression is crucial. This analogy to human behavior in different environments highlights the complex and dynamic nature of our microbiome.

items.title: Why Stripe Cut 500,000 Internal Docs Down to 5,000?
items.summary: What happens when AI agents start relying on the same messy docs your team already struggles to search? Demetrios hops into a Waymo in San Francisco with Dave Nunez, founder and CEO of Falconer and co-author of Documentation for Developers. They talk about why developers and agents need different things from docs, why agents sometimes skip up-to-date instructions, and how a stale internal document can contribute to a production incident. Dave shares how Stripe cut roughly 500,000 internal docs down to 5,000 worth maintaining. The conversation also covers how to capture the reasoning behind engineering decisions, when a diagram beats a wall of text, and who owns the fallout when an agent acts on bad information. items.title: Forged High Court Orders Led India To Block 129 Betting Websites In Two Rounds #Shorts #FrontPage
items.summary: India's Department of Telecommunications issued two website blocking directions this year based on forged orders impersonating the Allahabad and Rajasthan High Courts. The first, on July 21, covered 34 sites and the second, on September 2, covered 95, a total of 129 betting websites. Both orders carried official looking seals, the national emblem and QR codes.
